question: Prediction of conversion from MCI to AD within 36 months from structural T1 MRI in ADNI MCI participants. P-78: longitudinal DenseNet encoder + Transformer trajectory model, tested on held-out ADNI-1/2/GO (Dataset B) and external ADNI-3/OASIS-3 (Dataset A). P-84: 3D DenseNet-based Siamese classifier on native 1.5T or super-resolved ADNI-1 baseline scans. Same task, population class and channel (MRI); architecture, training data, input resolution and validation design differ, which the rule allows. The record's contrast (CSF p-tau/Abeta against a 2D CNN) is in neither paper; both papers are MRI-only.
metric: ROC-AUC with ROC-AUC (sensitivity and accuracy are also printed by both).

figures.P-78: Dataset B (held-out ADNI, 36-month status), single time point (STP): AUC 0.832 (95% CI 0.783-0.874), ACC 0.763 (0.711-0.816), SEN 0.852 (0.710-0.920) (Table 5; bootstrap CIs as printed). Dataset A (external ADNI-3 + OASIS-3, baseline scans): proposed network AUC 0.858 (0.803-0.918); the paper's own DenseNet baseline AUC 0.782 (0.709-0.842) (Table 3).
figures.P-84: ADNI-1, c-MCI (n = 77) vs s-MCI (n = 129), 36 months from the scan (Table 5, CIs as printed): 1.5T AUROC 0.553 (0.485-0.621), ACC 0.578, SEN 0.623 (0.557-0.689); c3T* AUROC 0.576 (0.508-0.644); d3T* AUROC 0.625 (0.557-0.693), ACC 0.650, SEN 0.675. A Hanley-McNeil check with 77/129 gives similar intervals: 0.553 [0.471, 0.635] and 0.625 [0.545, 0.705].

matched_figure_check: Two matched figures exist, and neither closes the gap. (1) Single-scan input at a 36-month horizon, which is P-84's condition: P-78's STP result on held-out ADNI, AUC 0.832 (0.783-0.874), against P-84's 0.553 (0.485-0.621) and 0.625 (0.557-0.693). The intervals do not overlap. (2) A DenseNet-type classifier on baseline scans, the nearest architecture to P-84's: P-78's DenseNet baseline on Dataset A, AUC 0.782 (0.709-0.842). Its lower bound is still above P-84's best upper bound (0.693). No figure in P-84 is under P-78's longitudinal condition.
performance_validity: Neither study meets the Section 3.5 exclusion. P-78's highest discrimination figure is QTP accuracy 0.907 (AUC 0.871), with external validation and bootstrap CIs. Its STP and Dataset A AUCs are 0.832-0.858. P-84's AUROCs are 0.553-0.625.

candidate_explanations.difference: Label and scan construction: in P-78 the sMCI group must be MCI at all time points, and pMCI can come from any MCI follow-up visit through 'dynamic data augmentation'. In P-84 s-MCI need only remain MCI 36 months after a baseline scan. A stricter stable group and non-baseline pMCI scans can widen class separation.
candidate_explanations.quote: subjects diagnosed with MCI at all time points are deﬁned as sMCI; subjects diagnosed with MCI at any follow-up visit and who progressed to AD within three years are deﬁned as pMCI. During the selection process for pMCI subjects, a dynamic data augmentation method was used
The c-MCI group was defined as patients who proceeded to be diagnosed with AD within 36 months of the MRI scan; the s-MCI group was defined as those who remained as MCI after 36 months of the scan.

candidate_explanations.difference: Training data and supervision: P-78 pre-trains on 1,393 ADNI subjects (6,313 scans) with CDR-SB supervision, and its ablation attributes 4.6 AUC points to CDR-SB. P-84 does not describe how its prognostic classifier was trained or split for the MCI task; it reuses the classifier built for AD classification.
candidate_explanations.quote: Binary classification between the s-MCI and c-MCI groups using 1.5T, 3T, and 3T* images was conducted with the aforementioned classifier to determine whether latent model-based SR enhances MCI prognostication.

candidate_explanations.difference: The CDR-SB supervision effect as P-78 reports it.
candidate_explanations.quote: The ablation study revealed that removing CDRSB reduced AUC by 4.6 % and accuracy by 6.4 %

candidate_explanations.difference: Input resolution and field strength: P-84's scans are ADNI-1 1.5T, native or super-resolved to 3T*. P-78 uses ADNI-1/2/GO scans registered to the MNI152 template resampled to 1.5 mm.
candidate_explanations.quote: For AD classification, those not in the superresolution cohort but with 1.5T MR scans during the baseline visit of ADNI-1 and those with only 3T brain MR images from the baseline visit of ADNI-3 were chosen.

candidate_explanations.difference: Architecture: a longitudinal CNN + Transformer trajectory model against a DenseNet Siamese classifier. P-78's own DenseNet baseline (AUC 0.782) narrows the gap but does not close it, so architecture alone is not shown to explain it.
Evaluation unit and sample: P-78's Dataset B is 101 subjects contributing 304 images. P-84 evaluates 206 patients.
candidate_explanations.quote: Ultimately, 101 subjects who met the above longitudinal criteria were selected from a total of 486 subjects, and 304 sMRI images were obtained, forming Dataset B.

reason: Both papers predict 36-month MCI-to-AD conversion from structural MRI in ADNI MCI. Their printed AUCs do not overlap, even under P-84's own single-scan condition: P-78 STP 0.832 (0.783-0.874) against P-84 0.553 (0.485-0.621) at 1.5T and 0.625 (0.557-0.693) after super-resolution. P-78's DenseNet baseline (0.782, 0.709-0.842) also lies clear of P-84's intervals. Candidate explanations are label construction, CDR-SB-supervised pre-training on a much larger training set, the undescribed training of P-84's prognostic classifier, input resolution and architecture; none is shown to be sufficient. The ledger record misreads both papers (CSF 77% vs 2D-CNN 82% sensitivity). This verdict rests on the figures the papers actually print, not on the record's.

quotes.quote: By utilizing structural magnetic resonance imaging (sMRI) data with ﬂexible time intervals, the proposed network quantiﬁes disease severity and predicts progression patterns in MCI patients over a 36-month period.

Single time point (STP) refers to a single follow-up diagnosis of MCI, while dual time points (DTP), triple time points (TTP), and quadruple time points (QTP) indicate multiple follow-ups at diﬀerent intervals over a three-year after the initial STP diagnosis.
The model was further evaluated to confirm whether it could distinguish c-MCI (n = 77) from s-MCI (n = 129).
